The foundational operators derive from classical conditioning theory where inhibition arises from stimulus interaction. The inhibitory stimulus compound (sIR) acts as a negative habit that suppresses positive responses when co-presented with reinforcing stimuli. Need reduction emerges from cessation of behavior generating a need, forming a feedback loop that reinforces inhibition. Reminiscence reflects temporal dynamics in memory consolidation, where prior learning effects resurface faster than typical decay rates. These primitives form a dual structure: one of active reinforcement and one of passive inhibition, both operating within a shared stimulus space. Failure modes include overgeneralization of inhibition or premature decay of need-driven behaviors. The mathematical framework supports recursive Bayesian updating for prediction and control of behavioral outcomes.
